items.statement: test_qp_ex_rc_bind_mw enters the case by creating QpExRCBindMw client and server players for a bind-MW operation followed by a deliberately denied remote write.
The test binds a Type-2 MW with a new local-write-only rkey, requires the bind completion to succeed, then posts an RDMA write with that rkey and polls its completion.
EOPNOTSUPP during extended-QP or Type-2 MW creation becomes SkipTest, while other creation errors are re-raised and successful allocation proceeds to bind the MW.
Both RC QPs are prepared to RTS before traffic, after which the server MW rkey is incremented and rebound before the client posts the remote write.
Each endpoint owns a device context, PD, MR, CQ, and RC QP; the Type-2 MW is retained by both its PD and the binding QP and is deallocated through MW.close.

The permission boundary is the full MR exposed through an MWBindInfo containing IBV_ACCESS_LOCAL_WRITE but no remote-write permission, and the oracle accepts only the exact remote-access-error completion.
The harness coordinates distinct client and server players by preparing each against the other's PSNs and QP numbers and synchronizing remote attributes before issuing work requests.
The raw CQ poll returns the first non-success completion, allowing the test to distinguish IBV_WC_REM_ACCESS_ERR from timeout and every other completion status.

RDMA access is authorized by the bound MW rkey and access flags: an RC RDMA write using an rkey bound without remote-write permission completes with IBV_WC_REM_ACCESS_ERR, without asserting any RoCE link-layer or routing rule.
items.description: A generic RDMA write posted with a local-write-only memory-window rkey must complete with IBV_WC_REM_ACCESS_ERR.
